Rape and sex-offender registries worldwide

Every sex-offender registry found, national to tribal and city, with the figures on rape by country. Click a dot, a country or a state. Some registries open inside this map; most US state and tribal sites forbid that, so they open in a new tab.

Rape, and the registries of sex offenders, worldwide

From the On-Planet Invasion page, (b)(i) Rape. The map shows every sex-offender registry found, at every level of government, and the figures on rape and sexual violence by country.

The registries

422 registries: 4 international, 83 national, 164 state, province, territory or city, and 152 US tribal nations. 255 can be searched by anyone. Click a registry's dot, its country or its state to see it. 72 of the registries' sites allow themselves to be shown inside this map; for those, "Show the registry here" opens the site in a panel over the map. The rest open in a new tab, because the site forbids being shown inside another page.

Each dot sits at the seat of the body that runs the registry (a capital, or a tribal government's town), not at any offender's home. This map copies no names or addresses of registered people: most registries' terms forbid copying them, and the registries themselves are where to search.

Counts of registered people are given only where the registry or a reliable source publishes one, with its date. Many registries publish none. Where a fact could not be checked, the box says so.

Countries with no registry in the sources checked are unshaded: that is not proof there is none. Still not covered (nothing found either way): Afghanistan, Algeria, Andorra, Angola, Azerbaijan, Bahrain, Bangladesh, Barbados, Belarus, Benin, Brunei, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cabo Verde, Cambodia, Cameroon, Central African Rep., Chad, Comoros, Congo, Côte d'Ivoire, Dem. Rep. Congo, Djibouti, Egypt, Eq. Guinea, Eritrea, Gabon, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Haiti, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Kiribati, Kosovo, Kuwait, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Lebanon, Lesotho, Libya, Madagascar, Malawi, Mali, Marshall Is., Mauritania, Mauritius, Micronesia, Moldova, Monaco, Mongolia, Mozambique, Myanmar, Nauru, Nepal, Nicaragua, Niger, North Korea, Oman, Palestine, Papua New Guinea, Qatar, S. Sudan, Seychelles, Solomon Is., Somalia, St. Kitts and Nevis, Sudan, Suriname, Syria, São Tomé and Principe, Tajikistan, Tanzania, Thailand, Timor-Leste, Togo, Tonga, Tunisia, Turkey, Turkmenistan, Tuvalu, Vatican, Venezuela, Vietnam, Yemen, Zambia, eSwatini.

States, provinces and cities checked where no register was found

  • Jalisco (MEX): A Registro Estatal de Agresores Sexuales (arts. 65-68 Ley de Acceso) passed committee 25 Nov 2020 (https://letrafria.com/aprueban-creacion-del-registro-estatal-de-agresores-sexuales-en-jalisco/), but the law text as of 22 Sep 2022 contains no such register. Later re-proposals reported (Mural). source
  • Tamaulipas (MEX): Initiative of 24 Nov 2025: 'Actualmente, Tamaulipas no cuenta con un registro estatal'; proposes a Registro Estatal de Personas Agresoras contra Mujeres, Niñas y Adolescentes. source
  • Roraima (BRA): Governor Antonio Denarium totally vetoed the bill creating a Cadastro Estadual de Pedófilos (Dep. Tayla Peres, PL 086/24). Whether the veto was overridden not verified. source
  • Catamarca (ARG): Bill of 12 Jun 2026 for a Registro Público Provincial de Personas Condenadas por Delitos contra la Integridad Sexual, motivated by 'la ausencia de mecanismos provinciales' to register such convicts. source
  • Northwest Territories (CAN): Hansard 16 Mar 2004 ('Registry Of Sex Offenders'): minister undertook to 'take a look at the issue of a registry and see whether or not that would work in the Northwest Territories' - i.e. no territorial registry then. Current status not verified. source
  • Canton of Solothurn (CHE): Cantonal government answer (RRB 2021/94) to interpellation I 0242/2020: 'Es besteht keine bundes- oder kantonalrechtliche Grundlage zur systematischen Publikation' of convicted sex offenders, and no cantonal legal room to create a public register. In 2014 the cantonal justice/police directors' conference (KKJPD) rejected a central register of dangerous offenders (https://www.srf.ch/news/schweiz/schweiz-kein-zentrales-register-fuer-gefaehrliche-straftaeter). source
  • San Juan (sex-offender register) (ARG): Mar 2026: prosecutor says no provincial law creates a register of sex offenders in San Juan; only a 2009 genetic-identification registry (recorded separately). source
  • Minas Gerais (BRA): Bill only. PL 4.841/2025 (public register of people convicted of crimes against sexual dignity) is attached to PL 4.513/2017, last moved 9 Dec 2025, no vote. Lei 25.508/2025 only bars such convicts from commissioned posts and creates no register (https://www.almg.gov.br/legislacao-mineira/texto/LEI/25508/2025/). source
  • Bahia (BRA): Bills only. Dep. Leandro de Jesus's register bill (still being pressed in Jul 2024) has no enacted law found; PL 26.263/2026 (Dep. Diego Castro, May 2026) is an anti-paedophilia policy with no register. The state law site legislabahia.ba.gov.br could not be searched from here. source
  • Ceará (BRA): Bills only: PL 867/2025, indicação 530/2023 (restricted Maria da Penha convicts register) and pi144/2026. The Assembly's thematic law index (Defesa Social, Direitos Humanos, Infância) lists no register law; the nearest is a ban on appointing people convicted of child sexual abuse (https://belt.al.ce.gov.br/index.php/legislacao-do-ceara/organizacao-tematica/defesa-social). source
  • Sergipe (BRA): No state register law or register bill found. Sergipe bills read in 2024–2026 deal with IML priority, campus harassment and a men's-responsibility campaign; none creates a register. The Assembly site blocks direct downloads from here. source
  • Rio de Janeiro (BRA): No state register law found. The only RJ bill seen (PL 3.291/2010, treatment of convicted paedophiles) creates no register and never became law. The ALERJ law database rejects search queries from this sandbox, so a full search was not possible. source
  • Acre (BRA): No law found. A full-text search of the Assembly's Legisla-e database (pedófilos, pedofilia, dignidade sexual, estupro, crimes sexuais, condenados, cadastro estadual, agressores sexuais) found only campaigns and Lei 3.497/2019 and Lei 4.577/2025, which bar people convicted of violence against women from public posts; no register. source
  • Tocantins (BRA): No law found. Searches of the Assembly SAPL database (laws from 2020 on) and the Assembly site search found no register; nearest is Lei 4.534/2024 on electronic monitoring of domestic-violence aggressors. Laws before 2020 were checked only through the site search. source
  • Roraima (BRA): No law found. The 2019 Cadastro Estadual de Pedófilos bill was vetoed in full (Folha BV, 7 Jan 2020) with no override found. A new bill, PL 086/2024 (Dep. Tayla Peres, 26 Apr 2024), would publish names and photos of people convicted of violence against women; its outcome was not found. Lei 1.486/2021 only bars Maria da Penha convicts from commissioned posts. source
  • Tierra del Fuego (ARG): No law found. The legislature's index of every law sanctioned 2001–2026 has no register law; Ley 1.523 (2023, protection of child victims of sexual violence) was read and creates no register. Register bills of 2006, 2016 and 2018 did not pass. source
  • Santiago del Estero (ARG): No provincial register law found in SAIJ (national legal database) searches by title and full text. The province joined the national genetic register (Ley 26.879) by agreement in Feb 2023. source
  • Santa Fe (ARG): No sex-offender register found. Ley 13.222 (17 Nov 2011, B.O. 23 Dec 2011) creates a general, confidential Registro Provincial de Huellas Genéticas Digitalizadas under the prosecution service for all crimes; it is not described as a sex-offender register, so it is left out. The owner may decide whether to show it. source
  • Jujuy (ARG): No provincial register law found in SAIJ searches by title and full text (integridad sexual, registro de violadores, datos genéticos, ofensores/agresores/abusadores sexuales) or in Spanish web searches. source
  • La Rioja (ARG): No provincial register law found in SAIJ searches by title and full text. The nearest laws are Ley 8.346/2008 (database of juvenile offenders) and Ley 9.718/2015 (protocol for child abuse victims); neither is a sex-offender register. source
  • Paraná (BRA): No Paraná state law creating a register was found in the Casa Civil database (searched for pedofilia, pedófilo, sexual, sexuais, estupro, estupradores, agressores, condenados, dignidade sexual), so the Santa Catarina bill's claim is not supported. Pending bills: PL 494/2025 (Alexandre Curi, rapists register) and a July 2025 bill by Dep. Mara Lima for a register of people convicted of sexual crimes against children. source

US county and city registries: 19 are on the map. Most US sheriffs publish theirs through one company's sites (OffenderWatch: sheriffalerts.com, communitynotification.com, icrimewatch.net), which refuse automated reading, so their full lists of agencies could not be collected here.

The figures on rape, by country

  • WomanStats Project: the Comprehensive Scale of Rape, 2018 (the page's map, footnote 41.5) and the officially reported rape prevalence scale, for 176 countries. Credited as WomanStats asks, for non-profit use. 11 countries came back without a value from WomanStats' feeds.
  • WHO: violence against women prevalence estimates for 2018 (published 2021, CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO) and 2023 (WHO Global Health Observatory), country by country: violence by a partner, and sexual violence by someone not a partner.
  • World Bank Gender Statistics (CC BY 4.0) and DHS survey results (credited as DHS asks): every indicator and year they publish on sexual violence.
  • DR Congo: the DHS surveys of 2007, 2013–14 and 2023–24 by province, and the 2011 estimates the page cites.
  • Left out until permission is given: the UN Office on Drugs and Crime's police-recorded counts of rape and sexual violence (24,466 rows for 161 countries). Its terms allow personal, non-commercial use "without any right to resell or redistribute".

The page's figures, checked against its footnotes

  • Footnote 41.1: pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7706187/
    The page says: “About 35.6% of women globally have experienced sexual violence”
    The source: “Globally, about 35.6% of women have experienced SV, with widely varying prevalence estimates [ 2 ].”; “[2] Garcia-Moreno C, Palitto C, Devries K. Global and regional estimates of violence against women: prevalence and health effects of intimate partner violence and non-partner sexual violence. Geneva: World Health Organization; 2013.”
    Matches: partly. The article does say 35.6%, citing WHO 2013. In WHO 2013 the 35.6% means physical and/or sexual intimate partner violence OR non-partner sexual violence ("Globally, 35.6% of women have ever experienced either non-partner sexual violence or physical or sexual violence by an intimate partner, or both."), not sexual violence alone. Newer WHO figures: 30% (2018 estimates), 31.6% / ~1 in 3 (2023 estimates); non-partner sexual violence alone: 6% (2018), 8% (2023). The article itself uses Global Burden of Disease prevalence by region (no per-country table).
  • Footnote 41.1: unicef.org/press-releases/over-370-million-girls-and-women-globally…
    The page says: “more than 1 in 8 girls under 18 are raped or sexually assaulted”
    The source: “More than 370 million girls and women alive today – or 1 in 8 – experienced rape or sexual assault before the age of 18, according to new UNICEF estimates released today.”; “When 'non-contact' forms of sexual violence, such as online or verbal abuse are included, the number of girls and women affected rises to 650 million globally – or 1 in 5”
    Matches: partly. Source says 1 in 8 girls and women alive today were raped or sexually assaulted before age 18 (a childhood-experience measure across all living females), not "more than 1 in 8 girls under 18". "More than" applies to the 370 million count.
  • Footnote 41.2: humboldt.edu/supporting-survivors/educational-resources/statistics
    The page says: “Only 2% of rapists (in the U.S.) are convicted and imprisoned; nearly 99% of perpetrators are male”
    The source: “Only 2% of rapists are convicted and imprisoned. (3)”; “3 U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee: Conviction & Imprisonment Statistics, 1993.”; “Nearly 99% of perpetrators are male. (1)”
    Matches: yes. Matches the page. Figures are old (1993 Senate committee; 2002 DOJ). Underlying 1993 report: 2.5% chance of conviction, 1.9% chance of incarceration per rape. See us_justice.json.
  • Footnote 41.3: house.mn.gov/comm/docs/2125c9c2-0bdd-4eb4-8719-2b628af6fd54.pdf
    The page says: “rape capital of the world, the Congo, an average of 48 women are raped per hour; quoted sentence on gang rapes ... children and babies”
    The source: “Congo is considered the rape capital of the world. On average, 48 women are raped every hour.”; “Gang rapes, genital mutilation, and sexual violence are committed by armed groups, gangs, and government and police forces. Many of the victims are children and babies.”
    Matches: yes. Quote matches except the section reads "by armed groups and gangs and by government and police forces" vs source "by armed groups, gangs, and government and police forces". The flyer gives no citation for 48/hour; it traces to Peterman et al. 2011 (AJPH) via the authors' brief: "approximately 1,152 women raped every day, or 48 raped every hour" - see drc.json.
  • Footnote 41.4: fightthenewdrug.org/how-porn-can-promote-sexual-violence/
    The page says: “as few as 1 in 3 and as many as 9 in 10 porn videos depict sexual violence or aggression”
    The source: “As few as 1 in 3 and as many as 9 in 10 porn videos depict sexual violence or aggression.”; “They analyzed hundreds of the most popular porn scenes and found that 88.2% contained physical violence or aggression. (Bridges et al. 2010, Violence Against Women 16(10))”; “45.1% of Pornhub videos and 35.0% of videos on XVideos depicted violence or aggression. (Fritz et al. 2020, Archives of Sexual Behavior 49(8))”
    Matches: yes. Exact match. Per the article, the upper figure (88.2%) is from Bridges et al. 2010 ("Aggression and Sexual Behavior in Best Selling Pornography Videos") and the lower (35.0%, XVideos) from Fritz et al. 2020. Not a country-level dataset.
  • Footnote 41.5: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rape_statistics
    The page says: “Rape of women in 2018 from WomanStatsProject (map)”
    The source: “Current page images include UNODC_Rape_statistics_2014-2023.svg and Rape_rate_per_100,000_-_country_comparison_-_United_Nations_2012.svg; no WomanStats file is in the current revision's image list.”
    Matches: partly. The WomanStats 2018 map is no longer on the current Wikipedia page. The matching map is on womanstats.org: "Comprehensive Scale of Rape, Scaled 2018" (LRW-SCALE-11), https://www.womanstats.org/substatics/LRW-SCALE-11-2018.png. Per-country values collected in womanstats.json. Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0; Commons file licence could not be checked (Commons API rate-limited this sandbox).
  • Footnote 41.6 / 41.7 / 48:
    The page says: “referenced in the section text”
